Document Title: CNN-Based Optimization of Paper Recycling through Automated Classification and Process Enhancement
Authors: G. Shasikanth; R. K. S; R. Jagadeesh Kannan; J. S. Kumar; M. Muthulekshmi; M. P

Abstract: Enhancing paper recycling using automated sorting systems is crucial for increasing recycling rates and minimizing environmental impact. This research introduces a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) methodology for the classification and optimization of the paper recycling process. We present a CNN model designed to identify and classify various types of paper trash, facilitating accurate sorting and reducing contamination. The data set comprises 10,000 images of diverse kinds of paper, including newspapers, cardboard, and office paper, sourced from an actual recycling centre. The model attained an accuracy of 94.5% in categorizing paper kinds, with a precision of 92.3% and a recall of 93.6%. The CNN-based approach exhibited a 30% enhancement in sorting speed relative to conventional human techniques. The automated system decreased contamination by 15%, resulting in superior output for recycling. The proposed method demonstrates substantial enhancements in operational efficiency and environmental sustainability, providing a scalable solution for paper recycling operations. These findings underscore the capacity of AI and machine learning (ML) to transform waste management and advance a circular economy.
